A.explanation: Divides $70.0\text{ cm}$ by 6 to get $11.7\text{ cm}$, which treats the spacing of minima as one full wavelength and miscounts the intervals.

B.explanation: Divides $70.0\text{ cm}$ by 5 to get $14.0\text{ cm}$, which treats adjacent minima as separated by $\lambda$ instead of $\lambda/2$.

C.explanation: Gives $70.0/3 = 23.3\text{ cm}$, which uses six $\lambda/2$ intervals for six minima instead of five intervals between them.

D.explanation: Five $\lambda/2$ intervals fit in $70.0\text{ cm}$, so $\lambda = 2 \times 70.0/5 = 28.0\text{ cm}$.

hints: Notice the incident sound wave and the reflected wave overlap between the loudspeaker and reflector to form a stationary wave, and the intensity minima marked M are the nodes.
Recall that in a stationary wave adjacent nodes, so adjacent intensity minima, are separated by $\lambda/2$, not by $\lambda$.
Count the minima from X to Y inclusive in the diagram and in the $70.0\text{ cm}$ distance to find how many $\lambda/2$ intervals fit into XY before calculating $\lambda$.
walkthrough: The forward wave from the loudspeaker and the backward wave reflected from the reflector superpose to form a stationary wave.
Sound intensity is minimum at the displacement nodes, so each M in the diagram is a node and successive M positions are $\lambda/2$ apart.
From X to Y inclusive there are six minima: X plus four passed through plus Y, giving $6-1 = 5$ node-to-node intervals.
Rearranging gives $\lambda = 2 \times 70.0\text{ cm}/5 = 140\text{ cm}/5 = 28.0\text{ cm}$ with unit $\text{cm}$, as expected for sound wavelength. This is option D.
